target: UTM-bundled QEMU/HVF, AArch64 PCI graphical guest, one vCPU
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-tosmisc-current-c161-deps-2026-11-12.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-demo-system-context --demo-system-path /Demo/AcctExample/TOS/TOSMisc.ZC --demo-system-module /Demo/AcctExample/TOS/TOSConfig.ZC --demo-system-module /System/Gr/ScreenCast.ZC --demo-system-module /Apps/Psalmody/JukeBox.ZC --demo-system-module /Apps/Psalmody/JukePuppet.ZC --demo-system-module /System/BlkDev/DiskCheck.ZC --demo-system-module /Demo/AcctExample/TOS/TOSMisc.ZC
verified: The current ISO booted to the graphical terminal and TOSConfig initialized the expected CD/C source configuration (tos-config=CD|C||).
TOSMisc DiskCheckAll skipped the source-backed C volume and returned without throwing; no physical data drive was mounted in this run.
DC2Doc recognized a system-font A with zero mismatch, preserved adjacent AZ glyphs, matched all 94 printable ASCII glyphs, and saved the dollar glyph with literal DolDoc encoding.
SoundShift removed an expired event; AUWrite wrote an 18-byte AU file and FileRead verified its timestamp and retained event.
GRWrite and GR2MV generated a one-frame MV file; GRRead reopened it and recovered the expected pixel.
ScreenCast toggled on/off, wrote a readable GR frame, and recorded the baseline/rest plus note-60 events into an AU file verified by FileRead.
MemTest completed its data-arena and separate code-arena stress loops and returned to the compiler.
not_verified: Full configured-drive and filesystem semantics beyond the separate RedSea fixture acceptance records, FAT32, and the destructive formatting workflow.
JukePuppet playback is covered by separate exact-image acceptance records, not by this run.
TOSDistro EFI image generation, live UTM interaction, physical Pi behavior, and physical audio capture/playback.
